purpose: Freeze public source inputs and their applicability boundaries for a future South African facility-resilience benchmark. This registry is not a facility tariff determination, project design, carbon-accounting statement, or live forecast.

sources.title: Medium-Term Budget 2026/27–2028/29, Annexure B: schedule of tariffs
sources.document_note: Annexure B describes the schedule as proposed and says listed tariffs exclude a 6 c/kWh network surcharge, a 2% surcharge on Business and Large Power Users, and VAT. Use as a documented source, not as proof of the tariff on a particular account.
sources.applicable_candidate_schedule: Business Conventional & Prepaid 400 V, <=100 kVA, subject to customer-class confirmation
usage_constraints: The official schedule and independent Focal Energy cross-check support one pair of fixed charges for the business block tariff up to 100 kVA: R890.45/month and R853.72/month; Focal labels the second amount as a capacity charge.

Augos' secondary JSON instead splits the fixed charges at 50 kVA and labels the second amount as a network charge, with R816.85/R783.16 for the >50-to-100 kVA band. This conflicts with the official schedule representation and must not be used for that band until reconciled.
The 6 c/kWh network surcharge in the City source and the 6 c/kWh DSM levy in Augos remain an additional unresolved naming/applicability conflict; neither is included in the calculator subtotal.
All usage remains candidate-only until verified against an approved current tariff and the actual customer's account/bill.
sources.claim_ceiling: Documented candidate tariff input for sensitivity analysis only; not account-verified.

monthly_charges_by_source.charge_as_published: second monthly fixed charge (column/meaning requiring confirmation)

sources.title: City Power Johannesburg — Business Conventional tariff database
sources.notes: Machine-readable tariff schedule includes 0.06 ZAR/kWh DSM levy; energy levels 3.9837/3.8052, 4.3370/4.1767, 4.5306/4.3799, 4.6871/4.5396 and 4.8228/4.6869 ZAR/kWh for high/low seasons respectively; monthly charge bands are captured in the primary source record. Values are secondary published tariff data; actual account class and tariff application still need confirmation.
sources.claim_ceiling: Secondary source cross-check and candidate inputs only.

sources.title: South Africa's 2024 Grid Emission Factors Report, Government Gazette notice 7891

factors.boundary: National generation emissions per end-user consumption; includes imported electricity adjustment; excludes transmission/distribution losses from the Scope 2 factor.

factors.intended_use: Government policy development and international reporting
factors.boundary: Domestic generation relationship; not interchangeable with the consumer NGGEF.
Transmission losses; applicability depends on supply arrangement.
Distribution losses; used with TLGEF for facilities not fed directly by transmission, according to report guidance.

usage_constraints: For consumer Scope 2 reporting, use NGGEF only within the reporting boundary described by DFFE.
These are annual historical location-based factors, not hourly marginal-emissions or dispatch-control signals.
Do not sum NGGEF, TLGEF and DLGEF unless a compatible Scope 3 accounting boundary specifically requires loss factors.
Keep the factor's reporting year and source digest attached to computed emissions.
sources.claim_ceiling: Official 2024 calendar-year reporting factors; not real-time/marginal dispatch emissions.

sources.title: PVGIS v6 API documentation
sources.documented_spatial_coverage: 75 degrees north to 60 degrees south; global longitude
sources.api_change_note: Documentation reports breaking changes on 2026-07-23: JSON response keys converted to snake_case and CSV headers changed.
inputs_required_before_site_run: mounting/configuration, tilt and azimuth as applicable
requested years or typical meteorological year choice
exact endpoint version, request URL/parameters, raw response and SHA-256
usage_constraints: Historical PVGIS data are not a current weather forecast.
Do not fill unknown rooftop shading, orientation, soiling or inverter clipping with unlabelled assumptions.
Preserve raw response bytes and parameter set; canonicalize separately if needed.
sources.claim_ceiling: Historical resource/PV estimate for a specified location and system configuration; not measured plant yield.

sources.title: City of Johannesburg Engages Stakeholders on Approved 2026/2027 Tariffs
confirmed_facts: City officials reported Council approval of the 2026/2027 municipal budget.
The City reported an approved average electricity tariff increase of 8.63%, effective 2026-07-01.
sources.limitation: This announcement confirms the budget approval/effective date and average increase, not the exact billing calculation for a particular tariff/account. Continue to treat the Business Conventional schedule arithmetic as candidate-only pending current approved schedule and account/bill confirmation.
sources.claim_ceiling: Official confirmation of the municipal budget/tariff effective date and average increase only.

sources.title: City Power electricity tariffs 2026/27: what Johannesburg businesses pay
relevant_claims: Business block tariff applies to standard 400 V connections up to 100 kVA.
The energy charges are described as a five-step block ladder over cumulative monthly consumption.
The cited fixed charges are R890.45/month service and R853.72/month capacity, and the network surcharge is separately stated as 6 c/kWh.
usage_constraints: Secondary source, not an account tariff determination.
Treat as a cross-check to the municipal schedule, not as a substitute for the official rate table or customer's billed tariff.
Its fixed-charge labels conflict with the Augos secondary tariff data and the disagreement must remain explicit.
sources.claim_ceiling: Independent industry cross-check for the candidate <=100 kVA business tariff and block semantics; not primary account billing evidence.

benchmark_protocol.baseline_fixtures: Keep the existing synthetic correctness and known-answer fixtures unchanged.
objective_boundaries: grid-energy cost with exact account tariff
location-based annual Scope 2 estimate using NGGEF where appropriate
battery sizing, round-trip losses and degradation only with a supported component model
outage survivability and longest continuous essential-service deficit
missing_inputs_that_block_site_specific_: customer-specific tariff and billed interval data
at least a documented meter/load time series
site coordinates and PV system assumptions
battery/inverter quotes, performance and lifecycle assumptions if economics include capex
external_comparators: REopt for matched facility generation/storage sizing and outage resilience
SAM for matched PV/battery dispatch and degradation modeling
PyPSA for scenario-aware capacity planning when time-series/model boundaries match
GenX only for planning cases with compatible spatial and temporal scope
benchmark_protocol.verification_rule: This registry does not make a site-real or outperforming-SOTA claim. Each data file must be versioned, source-attributed and digest-bound; unknown inputs remain unknown.
source_conflicts: Official budget / Focal cross-check: one fixed pair of R890.45/month and R853.72/month for <=100 kVA business block tariff; Focal calls these service + capacity charges.
Augos JSON: fixed-charge bands <50 kVA (890.45 and 853.72) and >50-to-100 kVA (816.85 and 783.16), with the second charge called monthly network charge.
Do not select the Augos upper-band values or decide whether the secondary fixed component is capacity or network without an approved tariff/account bill.
